quote.quote: This application was presented to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee on May 29, 2009.
A meeting of the Oncology Drugs Advisory Committee was held on May 29, 2009 to discuss ofatumumab for the treatment of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia who have received prior therapy.

recommendation.text: The committee voted 10 to 3 in favor: the majority agreed the Investigator-reported ORR of 42% (99% CI 26, 60) with a median DOR of 6.5 months was reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, supporting accelerated approval of Arzerra as a single agent in CLL refractory to fludarabine and alemtuzumab.

quote.quote: The majority (10 yes; 3 no) of the ODAC members agreed that the results of Protocol Hx-CD20-406 supported the accelerated approval of Arzerra®, as a single agent, for the treatment of patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

summary: The Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) met on May 29, 2009 and voted 10 to 3 that the investigator-reported ORR of 42% (99% CI 26, 60) with a median duration of response of 6.5 months was reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, endorsing accelerated approval of Arzerra in double-refractory (fludarabine- and alemtuzumab-refractory) CLL. Dissenters and the broader discussion raised concerns about likely overestimation of the response rate because CT scans were not obtained, inadequate toxicity evaluation, and inability to assess survival, and the committee recommended that CT scans be incorporated into disease assessment in future regulatory CLL trials. The review documents do not tie any of these concerns to a specific change in the Arzerra application: the committee's role was to endorse the accelerated approval, the CT-scan recommendation was directed at future trials rather than this product, and the post-marketing requirements (confirmatory trial OMB110911 on progression-free survival, an anti-drug-antibody assay, and a QTc study) are not described as resulting from an AdComm concern, so no concern-to-change linkage is recorded.
